summary: Lemma-level planning pass for all six layers. AA.0 owns restricted products of Haar measures and the absolutely convergent infinite rescaling required for Tamagawa measures; existing restricted-product carriers and topologies remain imported. AA.1 uses the pinned convolution points functor, finitely presented Hopf integral models and natural restriction of scalars. AA.2 fixes the character dual, nonnormal right-Haar quotient integration, central measurable Hilbert sections and number-field gauge/Artin normalization with basis-sensitive restriction-of-scalars Jacobians. AA.3 separates primitive GL_n/closed-orbit reduction from class-number consumers, parabolic integration, proper algebraic heights and fixed-K real Siegel containment. AA.4 separates arithmetic native-field approximation, algebraic neatness, actual quotient topologies, full/effective stabilizers, Hecke maps and restricted-product residual quotients. AA.5 checks the specified GL_1, GL_2 and quaternion levels. All stages are planned; none is closed. Missing mathematical inputs are exposed as exact gaps and supplier requests. The independent review/history remain unchanged pending a new independent review; no implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: The restricted product of countably many second countable groups is second countable
nodes.statement: Let ι be countable, let each G i be a second countable topological group and each B i an open subgroup of G i. Then Πʳ i, [G i, B i] is second countable. Consequently its Borel σ-algebra is generated by the boxes Π i, C i with C i open in G i and C i = B i for all but finitely many i.
hypotheses: ι is a countable index type
each G i is a second countable, locally compact, Hausdorff topological group
B i ≤ G i open subgroups
proofSteps: The finite subsets S of ι form a countable set, and Πʳ i, [G i, B i] is the union of the open subgroups U_S = Π_{i∈S} G i × Π_{i∉S} B i (RestrictedProduct.topologicalSpace_eq_iSup and the open embeddings of the principal pieces).
Each U_S is homeomorphic to a countable product of second countable spaces, hence second countable.
A space that is a countable union of open second countable subspaces is second countable; the boxes of the statement restricted to the U_S give a countable basis.

nodes.statement: For a number field K, the measure d^×x on the idele group 𝔸_K^× is the restricted product, through the topological isomorphism 𝔸_K^× ≅ Πʳ v, [K_v^×, 𝒪_v^×] (finite part) times ∏_{w|∞} K_w^×, of the Haar measures d^×x_v with vol(𝒪_v^×) = 1 at finite places, dx/|x| at real places and 2 dx dy/(x² + y²) at complex places.

proofSteps: Use RestrictedProduct.unitsEquiv for the finite part and its homeomorphism property for the units topology (GlobalNumberFields layer 6 proves local compactness and the units topology).
Apply restricted-haar-product with B v = 𝒪_v^×.

nodes.title: Products of form measures need convergence factors
nodes.statement: For K = ℚ and ω = dx/x on G_m, the local measures |ω|_p built from the additive normalization μ_p(ℤ_p) = 1 give vol(ℤ_p^×) = 1 - p⁻¹, and ∏_p (1 - p⁻¹) diverges to 0. Hence the family |ω|_p does not satisfy the normalization hypothesis of restricted-haar-product (cofinitely volume 1), and no rescaling by a single constant makes it do so; the Tamagawa measure of G_m uses the convergence factors λ_p = (1 - p⁻¹)⁻¹.
hypotheses: K = ℚ; the analogous statement for a number field K uses the pole of the Dedekind zeta function at s = 1
proofSteps: ℤ_p^× = ℤ_p ∖ pℤ_p has additive measure 1 - p⁻¹, and |x|_p = 1 on it.
∏_p (1 - p⁻¹) = 0 because ∑_p 1/p diverges (Nat.Primes.not_summable_one_div).
So the partial products of the volumes of ∏_p ℤ_p^× tend to 0 and the normalization condition fails at infinitely many places.
acceptance: This is the reason AA.2/tamagawa-measure inserts λ_v = L_v(X*(G), 1).
With λ_p = (1 - p⁻¹)⁻¹ the corrected measures are the normalized idele measures of idele-haar.

nodes.title: Adelic points of an affine algebraic group
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra H over a number field F, G(𝔸_F) is the group of F-algebra maps H → 𝔸_F under convolution (TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.points H 𝔸_F), with the topology of affine points over the topological ring 𝔸_F (weakest topology making every evaluation h ↦ x(h) continuous). Likewise G(𝔸_{F,f}), G(F_∞) = G(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ) and G(F_v). The diagonal ι : G(F) → G(𝔸_F) is mapPoints along F → 𝔸_F and the local projection p_v : G(𝔸_F) → G(F_v) is mapPoints along the projection 𝔸_F → F_v.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Evaluate the points functor on the F-algebras 𝔸_F, 𝔸_{F,f}, F_v (the adele ring is an F-algebra; the projections are F-algebra maps built from RestrictedProduct.evalRingHom).
Give each the affine-points topology supplied by RG2.0 for topological rings; it is a topological group because multiplication is composition with comultiplication and inversion with the antipode.

For H the GL_n coordinate ring, G(𝔸_F) is GL_n(𝔸_F) with the units topology.

nodes.title: Integral models over S-integers
nodes.statement: An integral model of H away from a finite set S of places of F (containing the archimedean places) is a finitely presented commutative Hopf algebra 𝓗 over the S-integers 𝒪_{F,S} together with an isomorphism of Hopf algebras F ⊗_{𝒪_{F,S}} 𝓗 ≅ H. hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
S a finite set of places containing the archimedean ones
proofSteps: Define the structure: the Hopf algebra 𝓗, the base-change isomorphism, and the map 𝓗(𝒪_v) → G(F_v) induced by 𝒪_v → F_v.

nodes.title: Spreading out
nodes.statement: Every finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra H over F has an integral model away from some finite set S of places.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Choose finitely many generators and finitely many polynomial relations for H. Over a field finite type is finite presentation.

Clear the finitely many denominators in the relations, comultiplication, counit, antipode and their polynomial identities. The resulting finitely presented S-integral Hopf algebra has the specified generic-fibre Hopf isomorphism.
acceptance: For H = F[GL_n] one may take S the archimedean places.

sources.match: Descent of finitely presented objects through the directed system of S-integers.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of integral models up to enlarging S
nodes.statement: Two integral models 𝓗, 𝓗′ of H (away from S and S′) become isomorphic, compatibly with their identifications with H, after base change to 𝒪_{F,S″} for some finite S″ ⊇ S ∪ S′. Consequently 𝓗(𝒪_v) = 𝓗′(𝒪_v) inside G(F_v) for all but finitely many v.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Apply Conrad, Theorem 3.4(3) to the two descents of the same finitely presented F-algebra, then to the Hopf structure maps.
For v ∉ S″ the isomorphism identifies the integral points inside G(F_v).
acceptance: The models 𝒪_{F,S}[GL_2] and its conjugate by diag(p, 1) agree away from S ∪ {p}.

sources.match: Uniqueness of models.

nodes.title: Integral points are compact open subgroups
nodes.statement: For an integral model 𝓗 away from S and a finite place v ∉ S, 𝓗(𝒪_v) is a compact open subgroup of G(F_v).
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: 𝒪_v is open and compact in F_v; by RG2.0 (Conrad, Example 2.3 and Corollary 3.7) X(𝒪_v) is open and compact in X(F_v) for X affine of finite type over 𝒪_v.
It is a subgroup because the group structure is defined over 𝒪_{F,S}.
acceptance: GL_n(ℤ_p) is compact open in GL_n(ℚ_p).

sources.match: Openness; compactness is Corollary 3.7.

nodes.title: Adelic points as a restricted product
nodes.statement: Let 𝓗 be an integral model of H away from S. The map x ↦ (p_v(x))_v is an isomorphism of topological groups G(𝔸_{F,f}) ≃ₜ* Πʳ v, [G(F_v), B_v], where B_v = 𝓗(𝒪_v) for v ∉ S and B_v = G(F_v) for the finitely many finite v ∈ S; and G(𝔸_F) ≃ₜ* G(F_∞) × G(𝔸_{F,f}).
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
𝓗 an integral model away from S
proofSteps: Points over a product of rings are the product of points; 𝔸_F = F_∞ × 𝔸_{F,f}.

Set-theoretic bijection: an F-algebra map H → 𝔸_{F,f} factors through 𝒪_{F,S′}-points of 𝓗 with values in 𝔸_{F,S′} for some S′ (H finitely generated, Theorem 3.4 limit argument), i.e. lands in ∏_{v∈S′} G(F_v) × ∏_{v∉S′} 𝓗(𝒪_v); conversely such a family glues (Conrad, Theorem 3.6).

Topology: on each 𝔸_{F,S′} the affine-points topology is the product topology (Conrad, Theorem 3.6, affine case), and both sides carry the direct-limit topology over S′ with open transition maps (RestrictedProduct.topologicalSpace_eq_iSup).
acceptance: For G = G_a it is FiniteAdeleRing as a restricted product (definitional up to the identification).
For G = GL_n it identifies GL_n(𝔸_f) with Πʳ_v [GL_n(F_v), GL_n(𝒪_v)].

nodes.title: Independence of the model and of the exceptional set
nodes.statement: The topological group structure on Πʳ v, [G(F_v), 𝓗(𝒪_v)] obtained from restricted-product-comparison does not depend on the integral model 𝓗 or on S: for two models the identity of G(𝔸_{F,f}) corresponds to the canonical isomorphism of RestrictedProduct.changeSubgroups, and enlarging S does not change it.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Two models give the same B_v for all but finitely many v (integral-model-unique).
Apply restricted-haar-change-subgroups (its topological part); both comparisons are compatible with the projections p_v, which determine the map.
acceptance: For G = GL_2 the models 𝒪[GL_2] and its conjugate by diag(p,1) give the same topology on GL_2(𝔸_f).

sources.match: Independence of the finite set; model independence follows from Theorem 3.4(3).

nodes.title: Adelic groups are locally compact
nodes.statement: G(𝔸_F), G(𝔸_{F,f}) and G(F_∞) are second countable, locally compact, Hausdorff topological groups.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: By restricted-product-comparison G(𝔸_{F,f}) is a restricted product of locally compact groups G(F_v) with compact open subgroups 𝓗(𝒪_v) for almost all v; apply RestrictedProduct.locallyCompactSpace_of_group and AA.0/second-countable.
G(F_∞) is a closed subgroup of GL_n(F ⊗ ℝ) for a faithful representation (RG2.0).
Hausdorffness follows from the closed-embedding property of affine points over a Hausdorff ring.
acceptance: GL_1(𝔸_ℚ) = 𝔸_ℚ^× is locally compact.
The full product ∏_p GL_n(ℚ_p) with the product topology is not locally compact; the restricted product is.

sources.match: Local compactness of the adele group.

nodes.title: Rational points are discrete in the full adeles
nodes.statement: The diagonal G(F) → G(𝔸_F) is injective, its image is a discrete subgroup, and the image is closed.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: F is discrete and closed in 𝔸_F (Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields discreteness).
For affine X, a discrete subring R ⊂ R′ gives X(R) discrete in X(R′) (Conrad, Example 2.2): choose generators h_1, …, h_n of H; the evaluation embedding sends X(R) into the discrete set R^n.
A discrete subgroup of a Hausdorff topological group is closed (Subgroup.isClosed_of_discrete).
acceptance: For G = G_a this is discreteness of F in 𝔸_F.
For G = SL_2 over ℚ, SL_2(ℚ) is discrete in SL_2(𝔸_ℚ).

sources.match: Exactly the statement.
Discreteness of principal adeles.

nodes.title: Discreteness in the finite adeles alone
nodes.statement: G(F) is discrete in G(𝔸_{F,f}) if and only if G(F) ∩ U is finite for one (equivalently every) compact open subgroup U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}). In particular G_a(F) = F is not discrete in 𝔸_{F,f}, SL_2(ℚ) is not discrete in SL_2(𝔸_{ℚ,f}) because SL_2(ℤ) is infinite, and ℚ^× is discrete in 𝔸_{ℚ,f}^× because ℚ^× ∩ ∏_p ℤ_p^× = {±1}.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: If G(F) ∩ U is finite then a smaller open neighbourhood of 1 meets G(F) only in 1, since G(𝔸_{F,f}) is Hausdorff.
Conversely a discrete subgroup meets the compact U in a finite set.
Compact open subgroups are commensurable, so finiteness for one U gives it for all.
Examples: ℤ ⊂ ℚ ∩ ∏_p ℤ_p is infinite; SL_2(ℤ) = SL_2(ℚ) ∩ SL_2(ℤ̂) is infinite; ℚ^× ∩ ℤ̂^× = {±1}.
acceptance: For a definite quaternion algebra D over ℚ, D^× is discrete in (D ⊗ 𝔸_f)^× modulo the centre (AA.5/definite-quaternion-compact).
Discreteness of G(F) in G(𝔸_F) does not imply discreteness in G(𝔸_{F,f}).

sources.match: Discreteness after projecting away a compact factor; the converse direction is the finiteness criterion.

nodes.title: Splitting off finitely many places
nodes.statement: For a finite set S of places, G(𝔸_F) ≃ₜ* G(F_S) × G(𝔸_F^S), with G(F_S) = ∏_{v∈S} G(F_v) and G(𝔸_F^S) the adelic points away from S; in particular G(𝔸_F) ≃ₜ* G(F_∞) × G(𝔸_{F,f}). The diagonal G(F) maps to the pair of diagonals.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Combine restricted-product-comparison with split-finite-factors, and points of a product of rings.
acceptance: For S = {∞} and F = ℚ, G(𝔸) = G(ℝ) × G(𝔸_f).

nodes.title: Functoriality of adelic points
nodes.statement: A homomorphism of affine algebraic groups φ : G → G′ over F (a Hopf algebra map φ* : H′ → H) induces a continuous homomorphism φ_𝔸 : G(𝔸_F) → G′(𝔸_F), x ↦ x ∘ φ*, commuting with the diagonals and with the local projections, with (id)_𝔸 = id and (ψ ∘ φ)_𝔸 = ψ_𝔸 ∘ φ_𝔸. Under restricted-product-comparison it is the restricted product of the local maps φ_v, which send 𝓗(𝒪_v) into 𝓗′(𝒪_v) for almost all v.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
φ a homomorphism of affine algebraic groups over F
proofSteps: Precomposition with φ* is a group homomorphism of convolution groups (TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.pointsFunctor).
Continuity: each evaluation of φ_𝔸(x) at h′ is the evaluation of x at φ*(h′).
φ* is defined over 𝒪_{F,S} for S large (hopf-spreading, morphism clause; integral-model-unique to compare with the chosen models), giving the restricted-product description (mapAlong_continuous).

The identity homomorphism induces the identity.

I a Hopf ideal of H

H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)

nodes.title: The centre on adelic points
nodes.statement: Let Z ⊂ G be the centre (centerDefiningIdeal). Then Z(𝔸_F) is a closed subgroup of G(𝔸_F) contained in the centre of G(𝔸_F), and Z(F) = Z(𝔸_F) ∩ G(F).
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Apply closed-subgroup-adelic to the centre Hopf ideal.
Points of the centre are universally central points (centerPointsSubgroup_eq_center), hence central in G(𝔸_F).
Intersection with G(F): a rational point lies in Z(𝔸_F) iff it vanishes on the defining ideal, i.e. lies in Z(F).

nodes.title: Restriction of scalars on adelic points
nodes.statement: For a finite extension E/F and an affine algebraic group G_E over E, with Res = Res_{E/F} G_E, there is an isomorphism of topological groups Res(𝔸_F) ≃ₜ* G_E(𝔸_E), natural in G_E, compatible with Res(F) = G_E(E) on diagonals.
hypotheses: E/F a finite extension of number fields
G_E an affine algebraic group over E
The Weil restriction and the completion/adelic base-change maps are the natural adjunction and canonical tensor-product maps; arbitrary point equivalences are excluded.
F is a number field and O(G) is a finite-type commutative Hopf F-algebra; integral generic-fibre identifications respect the Hopf structure.
proofSteps: Res(𝔸_F) = G_E(E ⊗_F 𝔸_F) by the defining property of Weil restriction (RG2.0a).
E ⊗_F 𝔸_F ≃ 𝔸_E as topological E-algebras (GlobalNumberFields layer 8).
Topologies: the module topology on E ⊗_F 𝔸_F is the one used by the affine-points topology (Conrad, Example 4.2).
acceptance: For G_E = G_m, Res_{E/F} G_m(𝔸_F) = 𝔸_E^×.
For E = F it is the identity.

nodes.title: Local unimodularity of reductive groups
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive group G over a local field E of characteristic 0, the locally compact group G(E) is unimodular.
hypotheses: E a local field of characteristic 0
G connected reductive over E
proofSteps: The modular character Δ : G(E) → ℝ_{>0} is a homomorphism, trivial on compact subgroups and on the centre Z(E), since Δ(g) is the modulus of conjugation by g.

Cartan decomposition G(E) = K M(E) K with M = Z_G(A) for a maximal split torus A (RG2.4 nonarchimedean, LieGroups layer 9 archimedean); so Δ is determined by its restriction to M(E), and M(E)/A(E)·M(E)^1 is finite with M(E)^1 compact, so Δ is determined by Δ|_{A(E)}.

For a ∈ A(E), the product ∏_{w∈W} w(a) of the relative Weyl orbit is W-invariant, hence a power of it lies in the split centre; Weyl representatives lie in K, so Δ(w a w⁻¹) = Δ(a), giving Δ(a)^{|W|·m} = 1 and Δ(a) = 1.
acceptance: GL_n(ℚ_p) and SL_n(ℝ) are unimodular.
The Borel subgroup of GL_2(ℚ_p) is not unimodular: Δ(diag(a,d)) = |a/d|_p^{±1}.

nodes.title: Compact open subgroups and product levels
nodes.statement: Every compact open subgroup U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) contains a product subgroup ∏_v U_v with U_v ⊂ G(F_v) compact open and U_v = 𝓗(𝒪_v) for all but finitely many v, and is contained in such a product; any two compact open subgroups are commensurable.
hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: By restricted-product-comparison and the box basis of the restricted-product topology (AA.0/second-countable), U contains an open box ∏_v V_v with V_v = 𝓗(𝒪_v) cofinitely; at the finitely many remaining finite v shrink V_v to a compact open subgroup U_v ⊆ V_v, using that G(F_v) has a neighbourhood basis of 1 consisting of compact open subgroups (requested from RG2.0), and put U_v = V_v elsewhere.
U is compact, so its projections p_v(U) are compact and U ⊂ ∏_v p_v(U), with p_v(U) ⊂ 𝓗(𝒪_v) for almost all v (U lies in finitely many translates of ∏ 𝓗(𝒪_v)).
Commensurability: U ∩ U′ is open in the compact U, hence of finite index.
acceptance: GL_2(ℤ̂) ⊃ K(N) = ker(GL_2(ℤ̂) → GL_2(ℤ/N)) = ∏_p K_p(N) is a product level.

hypotheses: F a number field
H a finitely generated commutative Hopf algebra over F (the coordinate ring of an affine algebraic group G)
proofSteps: Restricted-product condition (restricted-product-comparison).
For v with g_v ∈ 𝓗(𝒪_v) = U_v conjugation preserves U_v.
acceptance: For g = diag(p, 1) ∈ GL_2(𝔸_f), gGL_2(ℤ̂)g⁻¹ differs from GL_2(ℤ̂) only at p.

nodes.title: F-rational characters
nodes.statement: X*_F(G) is the group of homomorphisms G → G_m defined over F, realized as the group-like elements χ ∈ H (Δχ = χ ⊗ χ, ε(χ) = 1) under multiplication; χ acts on points by x ↦ x(χ) ∈ R^×. Equivalently, X*_F(G) is the Galois-fixed subgroup of the geometric character group X*(G_{F̄}).
hypotheses: F a number field
G = Spec H an affine algebraic group over F, H finitely generated
proofSteps: Group-like elements are units (inverse S(χ)) and form a group.
A homomorphism G → G_m is a Hopf map F[T,T⁻¹] → H, determined by the image of T, which is group-like.
Galois descent: an F̄-character fixed by Gal(F̄/F) is defined over F.
acceptance: X*_F(GL_n) = ℤ·det.
For E/F quadratic, X*_F(Res_{E/F} G_m) = ℤ·N_{E/F} while X*(Res G_m ⊗ F̄) = ℤ².

nodes.title: Modulus character of a parabolic
nodes.statement: For an F-parabolic P = M_P N_P of G (or any F-group with a normal unipotent F-subgroup N), δ_P : P(𝔸_F) → ℝ_{>0} is δ_P(p) = ‖det(Ad(p) | Lie N_P)‖, the idele norm of the determinant of the adjoint action on Lie N_P ⊗ 𝔸_F. It factors as ∏_v δ_{P,v}, is trivial on N_P(𝔸) and P(F), and δ_P(p) = e^{⟨2ρ_P, H_P(p)⟩}.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
P an F-parabolic with unipotent radical N_P (Tau Ceti dynamic parabolic P(λ) for an F-cocharacter λ)
proofSteps: det ∘ Ad|_{Lie N} is an F-rational character of P; compose with the idele norm (log-height).

nodes.title: Modular function of P(𝔸)
nodes.statement: For a parabolic P of a connected reductive G over a number field F, Mathlib's modular character (map (·p) μ_l = Δ(p)μ_l) on P(𝔸_F) is δ_P. With mutually inversion-normalized left and right Haar measures, dμ_l(p)=δ_P(p)⁻¹dμ_r(p). For a proper parabolic δ_P is nontrivial; for P=G it is 1.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: P(𝔸) = M_P(𝔸) ⋉ N_P(𝔸) (Tau Ceti Levi decomposition on points, AA.1/closed-subgroup-adelic); M_P(𝔸) and N_P(𝔸) are unimodular (AA.1/unimodular-reductive; N_P(𝔸) is unimodular as a restricted product of unipotent groups).
For a semidirect product M ⋉ N, right translation by m scales the Haar measure of N by the modulus of conjugation, which on N(F_v) is |det Ad(m)|_{Lie N}|_v.

Multiply over places: the modular character of the restricted product is the finite product of the local ones (AA.0/restricted-unimodular). Arthur's display on p. 25 has the inverse exponent; the GL_2 example on p. 21 fixes the sign used here.

nodes.title: Invariant measure on a coset space
nodes.statement: Let G be a second countable locally compact group, H ≤ G a closed subgroup with Δ_G|_H = Δ_H, and dg, dh right Haar measures. There is a unique G-invariant Radon measure dġ on the right coset space H\G with ∫_G f(g) dg = ∫_{H\G} ∫_H f(hg) dh dġ for every f ∈ C_c(G).
hypotheses: G second countable locally compact Hausdorff group
H closed subgroup
Δ_G restricted to H equals Δ_H
dg and dh are right Haar measures; invariance means the right G-action on H\G
proofSteps: Apply the positive-functional Riesz theorem on the canonical locally compact Hausdorff quotient. Regularity and finiteness on compact sets follow from the construction.

The averaging lift proves the stated C_c identity. For uniqueness, an invariant Radon measure λ gives the right-invariant positive functional f ↦ ∫ Pf dλ on C_c(G); its Riesz measure is a right Haar measure, hence c·dg by uniqueness of Haar measure applied after inversion (isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul), so λ and c·dġ agree on all Pf and, by surjectivity of P (bruhat-section), are equal. Invariance follows by comparing compactly supported integrals after right translation.
acceptance: For normal H, compare by inversion with the left-Haar extension construction IsSES.inducedMeasure; that declaration constructs a measure on the middle group from subgroup and quotient measures, and does not itself construct the general nonnormal quotient measure.
For H = G(F) discrete it is the measure of discrete-quotient-fundamental-domain.

nodes.title: L² space with a unitary central character
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 ⊂ Z(𝔸_F) be a closed subgroup such that 𝔛Z(F) is closed, and ω a continuous unitary character of 𝔛 trivial on 𝔛 ∩ Z(F). L²(G(F)\G(𝔸_F), ω) is the Hilbert space of (classes of) measurable φ on G(𝔸) with φ(γ z g) = ω(z) φ(g) for γ ∈ G(F), z ∈ 𝔛, and ∫_{𝔛G(F)\G(𝔸)} |φ|² < ∞, with right translation R a unitary representation of G(𝔸) on which 𝔛 acts by ω.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
𝔛, ω as stated
proofSteps: central-product-closed proves XΓ is closed from XZ(F) closed. The measurable associated-line and cocycle constructions identify equivariant functions with L² sections on XΓ\G.
The completeness node uses the section isometry to scalar L² and quotient invariance. The continuous equivariant-section density input supplies strong continuity of right translation.
The central action is multiplication by ω because X is central; the inner product is conjugate-linear in its first variable.

For G = GL_1 and 𝔛 = Z(𝔸) = G(𝔸) it is one-dimensional when ω is trivial on F^×, and zero otherwise.

nodes.title: Convergence factors from the character module
nodes.statement: Let X = X*(G_{F̄}) ⊗ ℂ with its continuous finite-image Galois action. For a finite place v, L_v(X, s) = det(1 - q_v^{-s} Frob_v | X^{I_v})⁻¹, and the convergence factors are λ_v = L_v(X, 1) at finite v and λ_v = 1 at infinite v. The partial Euler product L^S(X, s) = ∏_{v∉S} L_v(X, s) converges for Re s > 1, and ρ_G = lim_{s→1⁺} (s - 1)^r L^S(X, s) · ∏_{v∈S, v finite} L_v(X, s) with r = rank X*_F(G), whenever this limit exists and is nonzero.
hypotheses: F a number field
G = Spec H an affine algebraic group over F, H finitely generated
G connected
proofSteps: The Galois action on the character lattice factors through a finite quotient Gal(E/F), E a splitting field (Tau Ceti geometricCharacterGroup with its continuous Galois action).
Frobenius at unramified v (Chebotarev roadmap) gives the local factor.

When the action is trivial (G with split characters, e.g. GL_n or split tori), L(X, s) = ζ_F(s)^r by the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function (Tau Ceti dedekindZeta_eulerProduct_hasProd, Re s > 1) and ρ_G = (Res_{s=1} ζ_F)^r (Mathlib dedekindZeta_residue).
acceptance: For GL_n, λ_v = (1 - q_v⁻¹)⁻¹ and ρ_G = Res_{s=1} ζ_F.
For SL_n, λ_v = 1 and ρ_G = 1.

nodes.title: Tamagawa measure
nodes.statement: For a smooth connected affine F-group of dimension d for which the Artin leading coefficient ρ_G exists and is positive and the corrected integral volumes converge absolutely, define τ_G=|d_F|⁻ᵈ/²ρ_G⁻¹ times the convergent Haar product of μ_v=λ_v|ω|_v. At finite v, λ_v=L_v(X*(G_Fbar)⊗ℂ,1), including ramified inertia invariants; at infinite v λ_v=1. Use the specified additive normalizations dx, 2dxdy and vol(O_v)=1. Connected reductive groups satisfy the separate convergence target. If the geometric character lattice is zero, λ_v=ρ_G=1, but the gauge integral masses still need the convergent-product construction.
hypotheses: F a number field
G = Spec H an affine algebraic group over F, H finitely generated
G connected
ρ_G exists (convergence-factors)
ρ_G is finite and strictly positive
The product of corrected integral volumes is absolutely convergent and nonzero
proofSteps: Choose a finite exceptional set containing the bad models and all noncompact integral factors. At every good place compute a_v=λ_v|ω|_v(𝓗(O_v)) using weil-volume-formula.
Apply convergent-haar-product to normalize μ_v by a_v at every good place and then multiply by ∏a_v. Independence of the exceptional set and model follows from the corresponding AA.0 lemma.
Multiply by the fixed positive discriminant and Artin-leading-coefficient factors. No arbitrary factor parameters or finite-rescaling replacement enter the definition.

nodes.title: Tamagawa measures and restriction of scalars
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a finite extension of number fields and G_E a connected reductive E-group of dimension d. The canonical topological group isomorphism Res_{E/F}G_E(𝔸_F)→G_E(𝔸_E), together with the induced character-space map and its integral-lattice Lebesgue normalization, transports Tamagawa measures and norm-one quotient measures. In particular the Tamagawa numbers agree. The extension to connected nonreductive groups requires the Levi/unipotent integration input recorded separately.
hypotheses: E/F finite extensions of number fields
G_E connected reductive
The Artin leading coefficients and Haar products have the existence/convergence proved in the named inputs.
proofSteps: Choose an F-basis β of E and the coordinate determinant-line form Ω_β induced from an invariant E-form ω. The local comparison is |Ω_β|_v=j_β(v)^d∏_{w|v}|ω|_w, with j_β(v) defined by the actual Haar Jacobian, not by a bare local discriminant.
restriction-global-jacobian gives ∏_v j_β(v)=|d_F|^{[E:F]/2}|d_E|^{-1/2}. Its d-th power cancels |d_F|^{-d[E:F]/2} to give |d_E|^{-d/2}; an F-basis change cancels globally by the product formula.

artin-factor-induction identifies all local L-factors, including inertia at ramified places, and the leading coefficient and order of pole. The convergent restricted-Haar construction permits this regrouping.

F-rational characters of Res G_E correspond to E-rational characters of G_E; their norm evaluation and the character-lattice Lebesgue measures commute with the isomorphism. Quotient measure transitivity then identifies the norm-one rational quotient measures.
acceptance: For G_E = G_m: τ(Res_{E/F} G_m) = 1.

sources.match: The number-field torus normalization supplies the checked special case; the reductive extension is derived from the basis-sensitive and Artin inputs listed here.
This gives function-field compatibility as motivation; it is not used as proof of the number-field Jacobian.

nodes.title: Minimal rational parabolics and standard parabolics
nodes.statement: Fix a minimal F-parabolic P_0 ⊂ G with Levi decomposition P_0 = M_0 N_0, M_0 the centralizer of a maximal F-split torus S_0. A standard parabolic is an F-parabolic P ⊇ P_0; it has a unique Levi component M_P ⊇ M_0, unipotent radical N_P, and split component A_P = A_{M_P}. The standard parabolics are finite in number, correspond to subsets of the simple relative roots Δ_0, and every F-parabolic is G(F)-conjugate to exactly one of them.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Existence and conjugacy of minimal F-parabolics and maximal split tori, relative roots and the standard parabolics (Borel–Tits, requested from RG2.1).
Levi decompositions on points: Tau Ceti dynamic parabolics P(λ) = U(λ) ⋊ L(λ) for an F-cocharacter λ of S_0 in the positive chamber realise each standard parabolic.
A_P is the split component of M_P (AA.2/split-centre).
acceptance: For GL_n, P_0 is the upper triangular Borel, standard parabolics are block upper triangular and correspond to compositions of n.
For an F-anisotropic group P_0 = G and Δ_0 = ∅.

sources.match: Over ℚ: the parabolics containing a fixed minimal P_0 = M_0N_0 are rational, finite in number and represent all G(ℚ)-conjugacy classes; each has a unique Levi factor containing M_0, and A_P = A_{M_P}; for GL(n) they are the block upper triangular groups indexed by ordered partitions of n.

G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Restriction of characters X*_F(M_{P_2}) → X*_F(M_{P_1}) is injective; restriction X*(A_{P_1}) → X*(A_{P_2}) is surjective (Arthur §5); tensor with ℝ.

nodes.title: Admissible maximal compact subgroup of G(𝔸)
nodes.statement: A maximal compact subgroup K = ∏_v K_v of G(𝔸_F) is admissible relative to M_0 if K_v = 𝓗(𝒪_v) is hyperspecial for all but finitely many v, each K_v is a special maximal compact subgroup in good position relative to M_0 at finite v and a maximal compact subgroup of G(F_v) at archimedean v, and G(F_v) = P_0(F_v) K_v for every v.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Choose an integral model; for almost all v it is reductive and 𝓗(𝒪_v) is hyperspecial and in good position (RG2.3 request).
At the remaining finite places choose special maximal compacts in good position (RG2.4 Iwasawa), at archimedean places a maximal compact (LieGroups layer 9).
The product is compact by AA.1/restricted-product-comparison and Tychonoff.
acceptance: For GL_n, K = O(n) × ∏_p GL_n(ℤ_p) (Arthur §4).
The product of the local K_v is compact only because K_v = 𝓗(𝒪_v) for almost all v.

nodes.title: Adelic Iwasawa decomposition and integration formula
nodes.statement: For admissible K and standard P, G(𝔸_F) = P(𝔸_F)K = N_P(𝔸)M_P(𝔸)^1 A_P(ℝ)^0 K, and for f ∈ L¹(G(𝔸)), ∫_{G(𝔸)} f(x) dx = ∫_K ∫_{M_P(𝔸)} ∫_{N_P(𝔸)} f(nmk) δ_P(m)^{-1} dn dm dk for compatible Haar measures.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
K admissible
proofSteps: The factorization and the integrable-function formula are separate prerequisites.
Apply compact-factor Iwasawa integration first to compactly supported continuous functions, then to nonnegative Borel functions and the positive/negative parts of an integrable function.
acceptance: For GL_n over ℚ this is Gram–Schmidt at ∞ and GL_n(ℚ_p) = P_0(ℚ_p)GL_n(ℤ_p) at p.

nodes.title: The map H_P
nodes.statement: For standard P and admissible K, H_P : G(𝔸_F) → a_P is H_P(nmk) = H_{M_P}(m) for n ∈ N_P(𝔸), m ∈ M_P(𝔸), k ∈ K; write H_0 = H_{P_0}.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
K admissible
proofSteps: Extend each rational character χ of M_P to P by χ(nm)=χ(m). If pK=p′K then p⁻¹p′∈P∩K, and the positive adelic norm of χ is 1 on this compact group.
The resulting character logarithms descend along the open surjection P×K→G. This proves well-definedness and continuity without asserting an undefined M_P-height on N_P.

nodes.title: Class numbers of semidirect products
nodes.statement: If G = H ⋉ N over F with N unipotent, then every double coset G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U meets H(𝔸_f), and G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U is finite if H(F)\H(𝔸_f)/(U ∩ H(𝔸_f)) is finite for all compact open U.
hypotheses: G = H ⋉ N
proofSteps: Borel 2.4 and 2.7, using N(𝔸_f) = N(F)·(open subgroup) (unipotent-class-number-one) and that N(𝔸) is normal with G(𝔸) = H(𝔸) ⋉ N(𝔸) (Borel 1.6).

nodes.title: Arithmetic subgroups attached to a level
nodes.statement: For compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) and x ∈ G(𝔸_{F,f}), Γ_{x,U} = G(F) ∩ x U x⁻¹, viewed in G(F_∞) through the diagonal. It is a discrete subgroup of G(F_∞); for x, x′ and U, U′ the groups Γ_{x,U} and Γ_{x′,U′} are commensurable after conjugating by a rational element when x′ ∈ G(F) x U.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Discreteness: G(F) is discrete in G(𝔸) (AA.1/rational-points-discrete) and x U x⁻¹ is compact open in G(𝔸_f).
Commensurability: compact open subgroups are commensurable (AA.1/compact-open-product).

nodes.title: Component decomposition of a level quotient
nodes.statement: Let x_1, …, x_h represent G(F)\G(𝔸_{F,f})/U (class-number-finite). Then [g_∞] ↦ [(g_∞, x_i)] induces a homeomorphism ⊔_i Γ_{x_i,U}\G(F_∞) ≃ G(F)\G(𝔸_F)/U, equivariant for the right action of G(F_∞); the archimedean factor and the split centre are retained, and the finite set G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U is in general not the whole quotient.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
U compact open
proofSteps: Every (g_∞, g_f) is G(F)-equivalent to (γ⁻¹g_∞, x_i u) for unique i (Milne 5.13).
Injectivity on each piece: (g_∞, x_i) ∼ (g′_∞, x_i) iff g′_∞ = γ g_∞ with γ ∈ Γ_{x_i,U}.
Topology: U is open, so G(F)\G(𝔸)/U is a disjoint union of open pieces, each homeomorphic to Γ_{x_i,U}\G(F_∞).
acceptance: For GL_2/ℚ and K(N), the full rational class set GL_2(ℚ)\GL_2(𝔸_f)/K(N) is (ℤ/N)^×/{±1}; its pieces retain GL_2(ℝ). The φ(N) upper-half-plane components use GL_2(ℚ)^+ instead (AA.5). For N≥3 their number is twice the cardinality of the full rational class set.

nodes.title: Finite volume of G(F)\G(𝔸)^1
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive group G/F, G(F)\G(𝔸_F)^1 has finite positive volume for the invariant quotient measure. For a connected nonreductive group the same conclusion follows after supplying its characteristic-zero Levi decomposition, compact unipotent adelic quotient and the associated product integration.
hypotheses: F a number field
G connected
proofSteps: The norm-one part of the Siegel covering has finite measure by iwasawa-integration-compact and positive-root-cone-integral.
The quotient measure of its image is bounded above by this finite measure; overlap finiteness is unnecessary for this inequality.
Positivity follows from a nonempty quotient-open chart. The connected nonreductive extension is a separate Levi/unipotent input.
acceptance: For GL_1, vol(F^×\𝔸^1) < ∞ (GlobalNumberFields layer 6 compactness).
For SL_2/ℚ, vol(SL_2(ℚ)\SL_2(𝔸)) = vol(SL_2(ℤ)\SL_2(ℝ)) vol(SL_2(ℤ̂)) < ∞.

G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Finite by finite-volume; positive because the quotient measure of a nonempty open set is positive.
acceptance: τ(G_m) = 1 is finite.

nodes.title: When G(F)\G(𝔸) has finite volume
nodes.statement: For a linear algebraic group G over F, G(F)\G(𝔸_F) carries a nonzero G(𝔸)-invariant Radon measure of finite volume iff X*_F(G°) = 0.
hypotheses: F a number field
G linear algebraic over F
proofSteps: For connected reductive G the zero-character case is finite-volume, since its norm-one group equals the full adelic group.

A nonzero rational character gives a noncompact positive-real quotient. The split-centre product integration makes the volume infinite; merely pushing forward a measure does not justify a Haar conclusion.
Apply the separately recorded Levi/unipotent and component-quotient reductions for the stated general linear-group scope.
acceptance: GL_1(F)\GL_1(𝔸) has infinite volume; SL_n(F)\SL_n(𝔸) has finite volume.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Anisotropic groups have compact quotients
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G over F whose derived group is F-anisotropic (equivalently, G has no proper F-parabolic subgroup), G(F)\G(𝔸_F)^1 is compact.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
G^der F-anisotropic
proofSteps: Then P_0 = G, Δ_0 = ∅, and a Siegel set is ω·A_G(ℝ)^0·K with ω ⊂ G(𝔸)^1 compact; since K ⊂ G(𝔸)^1 and A_G(ℝ)^0 ∩ G(𝔸)^1 = 1, its intersection with G(𝔸)^1 is the compact set ω K (adelic-siegel-set).
siegel-covering-adelic gives G(𝔸)^1 = G(F)·(compact set).
acceptance: For a definite quaternion algebra D over ℚ, D^×(ℚ)\D^×(𝔸)^1 is compact (AA.5/definite-quaternion-compact).
For F^× this recovers compactness of F^×\𝔸^1.

sources.match: Compactness criterion (sufficiency).
The criterion for reductive groups.

nodes.title: Isotropic groups have noncompact quotients
nodes.statement: For connected reductive G over F with a proper F-parabolic subgroup, G(F)\G(𝔸_F)^1 is not compact. Precisely: G(F)\G(𝔸)^1 is compact iff G(F) has no nontrivial unipotent element iff G^der is F-anisotropic.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: A proper F-parabolic gives a nontrivial F-split torus S ⊄ Z(G) and a nontrivial unipotent u ∈ N_P(F) (Borel–Tits, RG2.1).

Take S inside G^der and a ∈ S(F_v) at an archimedean v with a^n u a^{-n} → 1 in G(F_v); view a as the adele supported at v, so a ∈ G(𝔸)^1. If γ_n a^{-n} → x in G(𝔸)^1, the rational elements γ_n u γ_n⁻¹ = (γ_n a^{-n})(a^n u a^{-n})(γ_n a^{-n})⁻¹ converge to x u′ x⁻¹, where u′ is 1 at v and u elsewhere. By discreteness they are eventually equal to one c ∈ G(F) with c_v = 1, so c = 1 and u = 1, a contradiction (Mahler-type argument).
The equivalences with the unipotent and anisotropy conditions are Borel–Tits (RG2.1).
acceptance: SL_2(ℚ)\SL_2(𝔸) is not compact; the sequence diag(n, 1/n) at ∞ escapes.

sources.match: Compactness criterion (necessity).

nodes.title: Cocompact arithmetic groups contain no unipotents
nodes.statement: Let G be connected semisimple over ℚ and Γ = G(ℚ) ∩ U for a compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_f). If Γ\G(ℝ) is compact then Γ contains no nontrivial unipotent element.
hypotheses: G connected semisimple over ℚ
U compact open
proofSteps: By component-decomposition and finite index arguments, Γ\G(ℝ) is compact iff G(ℚ)\G(𝔸) is compact.
Apply compactness-isotropic: a nontrivial unipotent in Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) makes G isotropic, hence the quotient noncompact.
acceptance: SL_2(ℤ)\SL_2(ℝ) is noncompact and SL_2(ℤ) contains (1 1; 0 1).
For a definite quaternion algebra the unit groups are finite and contain no unipotents.

sources.match: The statement, proved here for arithmetic Γ from the compactness criterion.

nodes.title: S-arithmetic subgroups are lattices
nodes.statement: Let G be connected semisimple over F, S a finite set of places containing the archimedean ones, and U^S ⊂ G(𝔸_F^S) compact open. Then Γ_S = G(F) ∩ G(F_S)U^S is a lattice in G(F_S) = ∏_{v∈S} G(F_v), cocompact iff G is F-anisotropic.
hypotheses: G connected semisimple over F
S finite ⊇ archimedean places
proofSteps: G(F)\G(F)(G(F_S) × U^S) is open and closed in G(F)\G(𝔸) and equals Γ_S\(G(F_S) × U^S); dividing by the right action of U^S gives Γ_S\G(F_S), with fibres copies of U^S (as in component-decomposition with S in place of the archimedean places). By class-number-finite, G(F)\G(𝔸) is a finite union of such pieces for translates x_iU^Sx_i⁻¹, whose arithmetic groups are commensurable with Γ_S.
An open subset of a finite-volume space has finite volume (finite-volume); compactness by compactness-anisotropic and compactness-isotropic.
acceptance: SL_2(ℤ[1/p]) is a lattice in SL_2(ℝ) × SL_2(ℚ_p).

sources.match: S-arithmetic lattices, used in the proof of strong approximation.

nodes.title: Height functions on G(𝔸)
nodes.statement: Choose a faithful F-algebraic representation r : G → GL_m containing a representation and its dual (and, if needed, a trivial summand), so the resulting height is proper and each local norm is at least 1. Define ‖x‖_r = product over v of ‖r(x)_v‖_v, using the entrywise maximum of normalized absolute values at finite v and the Hilbert–Schmidt norm raised to the archimedean multiplicity [F_v:ℝ] at infinity. The height is submultiplicative, has compact sublevel sets, and satisfies polynomial inverse and rational-point counting bounds, subject to the recorded proper-height and counting inputs.
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
r is an algebraic faithful representation chosen with the stated dual/properness condition; arbitrary abstract faithful point representations do not suffice
proofSteps: Use the actual closed algebraic embedding augmented by its dual; the normalized local norms are at least one and equal one at almost all finite places.
Finite matrix maximum norms and infinite Hilbert–Schmidt norms are submultiplicative. Polynomial coordinate comparison bounds the inverse.
Properness is adelic-height-proper. Each rational coordinate projective height is bounded by a power of the group height; rational-coordinate-height-count supplies the polynomial count.
acceptance: For GL_1/ℚ with r(x)=diag(x,x⁻¹), ‖x‖ = sqrt(|x∞|²+|x∞|⁻²) times product over finite v of max(|x_v|_v,|x_v|_v⁻¹).

sources.match: Exactly the height.

uses.how: moderate growth and polynomial comparability (RS-04: AA.3 owns the height comparison)
rapid decay |φ(x)| ≤ C‖x‖^{-N} on Siegel sets

nodes.statement: For two proper F-algebraic height representations r,r′ satisfying adelic-height, there are C,N>0 with ‖x‖_{r′}≤C‖x‖_r^N for every x∈G(𝔸_F), and conversely. Multiplication on either side by a fixed compact subgroup changes these heights by bounded factors.

G a connected reductive group over F
Both representations are algebraic and define proper heights controlling their inverses
proofSteps: Multiply the local polynomial comparisons; only finitely many c_v differ from one.
Use submultiplicativity for bounded height and inverse-height on the compact subgroup. Generic adelic comparison belongs here; AF.1 consumes it.

nodes.statement: On a Siegel set 𝔖(T_1, ω) there are c, C > 0 such that for x = pak, c^{-1} e^{c‖H_0(a)‖} ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ C e^{C‖H_0(a)‖} (any norm on a_0); in particular log‖x‖ and ‖H_0(x)‖ are comparable on 𝔖 ∩ G(𝔸)^1 up to constants.

G a connected reductive group over F
proofSteps: Write r(pak) = r(p) r(a) r(k): r(p), r(k) lie in compact sets; r(a) is diagonalizable with eigenvalues e^{λ(H_0(a))} for the weights λ of r.

nodes.title: Horospherical decomposition for a fixed maximal compact
nodes.statement: Let G be connected semisimple over ℚ, G = G(ℝ)^+, K ⊂ G maximal compact with Cartan involution θ, and 𝐏 a ℚ-parabolic with unipotent radical 𝐍_P and Levi quotient 𝐋_P. With S_P the split centre of 𝐋_P, A_P = S_P(ℝ)^0 and M_P the real points of ⋂_{χ∈X*(𝐋_P)} ker χ², there is a unique θ-stable real Levi lift of (𝐋_P)_ℝ, giving P = N_P A_P M_P and the diffeomorphism N_P × A_P × ((M_P ∩ G) K) → G (M_P itself can leave G(ℝ)^+: for PGL_2 it contains diag(−1, 1)). Left multiplication by p_0 = n_0 a_0 m_0 acts by (n, a, m) ↦ (n_0 · (a_0m_0) n (a_0m_0)⁻¹, a_0 a, m_0 m).
hypotheses: G connected semisimple over ℚ
K a maximal compact subgroup of G(ℝ)^+
𝐏 a ℚ-parabolic
proofSteps: θ-stable Levi lift: Borel–Serre 1.9 (cited by BKT).
The decomposition G = P K (real Iwasawa decomposition, LieGroups layer 9) and P = N_P ⋊ L_P with L_P = A_P × M_P.
The action formula is the conjugation computation; BKT print 'right action', corrected to left action (source issue).
For K′=uKu⁻¹ write g=puk u⁻¹, so gu=pu k. Right multiplication of p by u∈N_P leaves its A-coordinate fixed. This proves the stated change-of-basepoint formula.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℝ), K = SO(2), 𝐏 upper triangular: N_P = {n(x)}, A_P = {diag(a^{1/2}, a^{-1/2})}, M_P = {±1}.
Changing K changes the Levi lift by conjugation by an element of N_P.

For t > 0, A_{P,t} = {a ∈ A_P : a^α > t for all α ∈ Δ(A_P, N_P)}, and e_P(a) = (a^{-α_1}, …, a^{-α_r}) is a semialgebraic diffeomorphism A_P ≃ (ℝ_{>0})^r with e_P(A_{P,t}) = (0, 1/t)^r.

e_P is the composite of the logarithm and the dual basis of Δ.

For g ∈ G, 𝔖g is a Siegel set for 𝐏 and g⁻¹Kg, and for g ∈ 𝐏(ℝ), g𝔖 is a Siegel set for 𝐏 and K (exactly, for the sets U a A_{>0} W of the erratum; for Definition 2.3's A_{P,t}, up to containment). nodes.statement: For an arithmetic subgroup Γ ⊂ 𝐆(ℚ), there are only finitely many Γ-conjugacy classes of ℚ-parabolic subgroups.
hypotheses: G connected semisimple over ℚ
Γ arithmetic
proofSteps: Every ℚ-parabolic is 𝐆(ℚ)-conjugate to a standard one (minimal-parabolic-data).
𝐆(ℚ) = ⊔_{finite} Γ g_i 𝐏(ℚ) for each standard 𝐏 (Borel 7.3: finiteness of G_ℤ\(G/P)_ℚ, via class-number-finite for the adelic form).
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ) there is one cusp; for Γ_0(p), two.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.
The finiteness behind it.

nodes.title: Finitely many fixed-K Siegel sets cover
nodes.statement: Let 𝐏_1, …, 𝐏_k represent the Γ-conjugacy classes of ℚ-parabolics and K a fixed maximal compact. There are Siegel sets 𝔖_i = U_i × A_{𝐏_i,t_i} × W_i associated to 𝐏_i and the same K whose images cover Γ\G/M.
hypotheses: G connected semisimple over ℚ
Γ arithmetic
K fixed, M ⊂ K compact
proofSteps: Obtain a covering G = ⋃_i Γ𝔖′_i by Siegel sets that all use one common maximal compact K′ (Borel–Ji Proposition 2.5 with a single base point, valid by erratum §1.1; or step 2). Write K′ = gKg⁻¹ for one g ∈ G. Since Gg = G, G = ⋃_i Γ(𝔖′_i g), and by real-siegel-translation each 𝔖′_i g is a Siegel set for 𝐏_i and K. Enlarging U_i, W_i cannot replace this single right translation: erratum §1.6.1 shows a Siegel set for one maximal compact is not covered by finitely many translates of Siegel sets for another.
The adelic covering siegel-covering-adelic projected to the archimedean component gives the same conclusion.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ), one Siegel set {|x| ≤ 1/2, y ≥ √3/2} covers.

sources.match: As printed with base points x_i.
The fixed-K correction.

nodes.title: Finite overlaps of Siegel sets
nodes.statement: For Siegel sets 𝔖_1, 𝔖_2 associated to the same K, the set {γ ∈ Γ : γ𝔖_1 ∩ 𝔖_2 ≠ ∅} is finite; the same holds for the relatively compact closures of their unipotent and Levi factors.
hypotheses: as in real-siegel-finite-cover
proofSteps: Use the real reductive fundamental-set construction Borel–Harish-Chandra §6.5 and Borel §3.4, based on closed-orbit-lattice-finite and GL_n real overlap.

Transfer to the specified parabolic Siegel sets through the fixed-K convention comparison and the rational containment contract. The exact transfer is a remaining refinement, not an appeal back to adelic overlap.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ) and Σ = {|x| ≤ 1/2, y ≥ √3/2}, exactly ten γ up to sign: 1, T^{±1}, S, ST^{±1}, T^{±1}S, TST and T⁻¹ST⁻¹.

sources.match: Exactly the statement (for one fixed K).

nodes.title: Inequivalent cusps separate
nodes.statement: If 𝐏_1 and 𝐏_2 are not Γ-conjugate, then for fixed U_i, W_i and all sufficiently large t_1, t_2, γ𝔖_1 ∩ 𝔖_2 = ∅ for every γ ∈ Γ.
hypotheses: as in real-siegel-finite-cover
proofSteps: By real-siegel-finite-overlap only finitely many γ are relevant; for each, γ𝐏_1γ⁻¹ ≠ 𝐏_2, and deep parts of Siegel sets for different parabolics are disjoint (deep-distinct-parabolics).
acceptance: For Γ_0(p), the Siegel sets at the two cusps ∞ and 0 are disjoint modulo Γ_0(p) once t is large.

sources.match: As printed the quantifier on γ is missing; corrected to 'for all γ ∈ Γ' (source issue).

nodes.title: Deep self-intersections come from the parabolic
nodes.statement: For fixed U, W and sufficiently large t, a Siegel set 𝔖 for 𝐏 and K satisfies γ𝔖 ∩ 𝔖 = ∅ for every γ ∈ Γ ∖ Γ_𝐏, where Γ_𝐏 = Γ ∩ 𝐏(ℚ).
hypotheses: as in real-siegel-finite-cover
proofSteps: Finitely many candidates γ by real-siegel-finite-overlap; for γ ∉ 𝐏, γ𝐏γ⁻¹ ≠ 𝐏 and deep-distinct-parabolics applies to γ𝔖 (a Siegel set for γ𝐏γ⁻¹, real-siegel-translation).
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ) and t > 1, only the translations ±T^n map the horoball {y > t} to itself.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Deep Siegel sets of distinct parabolics are disjoint
nodes.statement: For distinct ℚ-parabolics 𝐏_1 ≠ 𝐏_2 and fixed bounded U_i, W_i (one K), the Siegel sets 𝔖_1, 𝔖_2 are disjoint once t_1, t_2 are sufficiently large.
hypotheses: as in real-siegel-finite-cover
proofSteps: After exchanging 𝐏_1 and 𝐏_2 if necessary (needed when 𝐏_1 ⊋ 𝐏_2: for SL_3 with 𝐏_1 maximal and 𝐏_2 the Borel, the root of 𝐏_1 is unbounded on 𝔖_2), in horospherical coordinates of 𝐏_1, points of 𝔖_2 have A_{𝐏_1}-coordinate bounded in the direction of some simple root (Borel–Ji 2.5(5), using the relative Bruhat decomposition of 𝐏_1 and 𝐏_2).
acceptance: For SL_2, the horoballs at two distinct rational cusps are disjoint for large t.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Comparison of Siegel-set conventions
nodes.statement: Fix K. Every Siegel set U × A_{P,t} × W associated to 𝐏 and K is contained in a Siegel set Ω A_{t′} K in Orr's sense for a Siegel triple (𝐏_0, 𝐒_0, K) with 𝐏_0 ⊂ 𝐏 a minimal ℚ-parabolic, and conversely; every Siegel set for K lies in a 𝐆(ℚ)-translate of one for K and a fixed minimal ℚ-parabolic.
hypotheses: as in real-siegel-set
proofSteps: Write m ∈ W as n′a′m′k′ in M_P relative to 𝐏_0 ∩ 𝐋_P; A_P is central in L_P, so u a m k = (u n′)(a a′) m′ (k′ k), and the simple roots of 𝐏_0 are bounded below on a a′ because a′ ranges in a compact set.
The last statement: all minimal ℚ-parabolics are 𝐆(ℚ)-conjugate (minimal-parabolic-data) and real-siegel-translation.
acceptance: For SL_2 the two conventions coincide.

sources.match: The two conventions (Borel–Ji and Borel/Orr); the bridge is recorded in the reviewed extraction PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20.

Orr's Siegel triples (minimal rational parabolic, the unique real torus stable under the Cartan involution of K and conjugate to a maximal rational split torus, and K), Siegel sets ΩA_tK, and how they compare with Borel's and AMRT's conventions.

nodes.title: Containment of subgroup Siegel sets
nodes.statement: Let 𝐇 ⊂ 𝐆 be reductive ℚ-groups, (𝐏_H, 𝐒_H, K_H) a Siegel triple for 𝐇 and 𝔖_H = Ω A_t K_H a Siegel set. Let K_G ⊂ 𝐆(ℝ) be maximal compact with K_H ⊂ K_G and whose Cartan involution stabilises 𝐒_H. Then there are a Siegel triple (𝐏_G, 𝐒_G, K_G), a Siegel set 𝔖_G for it and a finite C ⊂ 𝐆(ℚ) with 𝔖_H ⊂ C·𝔖_G; moreover R_u(𝐏_H) ⊂ R_u(𝐏_G) and 𝐒_H = 𝐒_G ∩ 𝐇.
hypotheses: 𝐇 ⊂ 𝐆 reductive over ℚ
K_H ⊂ K_G
θ_{K_G} stabilises 𝐒_H
proofSteps: Reduce to S_H ℚ-split: choose u ∈ R_u(𝐏_H)(ℝ) with uS_Hu⁻¹ ℚ-split; 𝔖_H u⁻¹ is a Siegel set for (𝐏_H, uS_Hu⁻¹, uK_Hu⁻¹), the Cartan involution of uK_Gu⁻¹ stabilises uS_Hu⁻¹, and if 𝔖_H u⁻¹ ⊂ C·𝔖′_G then 𝔖_H ⊂ C·(𝔖′_G u), a Siegel set for (𝐏_G, u⁻¹S′_Gu, K_G) because u ∈ R_u(𝐏_H) ⊂ R_u(𝐏_G) (Orr §4.1). Then, for h=μak, choose the admissible w putting a in wA_{G,t′}w⁻¹.
Write w′_Q⁻¹μ=νw_K⁻¹bλ using containment-compact-factors. Since λ∈Z_G(S_H), it commutes with a.

The finitely many compact b-factors have all simple-root values bounded below by a common s>0; hence w_K⁻¹ba w_K∈A_{G,t′s}. Thus h∈w′_Q Ω_G A_{G,t′s}K_G. Take the finite rational set of w′_Q, as Orr §4.6 Proposition 4.14, with the 2023 correction.
acceptance: For 𝐇 = 𝐆 it is trivial with C = {1}.

sources.match: The fixed-K theorem requires Cartan stability of S_H.
The compact-factor calculation completes the finite rational containment.
Reduction of the containment theorem to a rationally split subgroup torus by a unipotent conjugation, undone by a right translation of the resulting Siegel set.

nodes.title: Stability of the subgroup under the Cartan involution suffices
nodes.statement: In the setting of orr-schnell-containment with K_H ⊂ K_G: if the Cartan involution Θ of 𝐆 for K_G stabilises 𝐇, then Θ|_𝐇 is the Cartan involution of 𝐇 for K_H and Θ stabilises the torus 𝐒_H of every Siegel triple, so the theorem applies. The converse fails for 𝐆 = SL_2, 𝐇 = {(a, db; b, a) : a² − db² = 1} with d a positive non-square rational, K_G = SO_2(ℝ), 𝐒_H = {1}.
hypotheses: as in orr-schnell-containment
proofSteps: A Cartan involution of 𝐆 stabilising 𝐇 restricts to one of 𝐇 (uniqueness of Cartan involutions up to conjugacy fixing K_H).
Counterexample: 𝐇(ℝ) is a split torus not stable under transpose-inverse, but 𝐒_H = {1} is.
acceptance: The counterexample: transpose-inverse sends (a, db; b, a) to (a, −b; −db, a), not in 𝐇 for d ≠ 1.

sources.match: The sufficient condition; the counterexample to the converse is Orr–Schnell Remark 2 as recorded in the reviewed extraction.
Stability of H under the Cartan involution of K_G implies the torus condition; the norm-one torus of a real quadratic field inside SL_2 shows the converse fails.

nodes.title: Intersecting Siegel sets with a subgroup
nodes.statement: Let 𝐇 ⊂ 𝐆 be reductive over ℚ, K_H = K_G ∩ 𝐇(ℝ) maximal compact, and assume every K_H-Siegel set lies in finitely many 𝐆(ℚ)-translates of a K_G-Siegel set (the conclusion of orr-schnell-containment). Then for every K_G-Siegel set 𝔖_G there are a K_H-Siegel set 𝔖_H and a finite F ⊂ 𝐇(ℚ) with 𝔖_G ∩ 𝐇(ℝ) ⊂ F 𝔖_H.
hypotheses: as stated, with the forward-containment hypothesis
proofSteps: Choose arithmetic groups Γ_H⊂Γ_G compatible with the rational embedding and a finite Siegel cover H(ℝ)=Γ_H C_HΣ_H.
The containment hypothesis gives Σ_H⊂AΣ_G with A⊂G(ℚ) finite. Any γ_H C_HΣ_H meeting the given Σ_G determines a Γ_G-overlap between two fixed rational translates of Σ_G.

The real Siegel property bounds these overlap elements by a finite set. Retain their H-rational factors to obtain the desired finite H(ℚ)-translates of Σ_H. This is Proposition 28.1, rather than a conclusion of Borel–Harish-Chandra 7.5.
acceptance: For 𝐇 = 𝐆 it is trivial.

sources.match: This supplies the rational finite-translate preimage statement.
The erratum replaces the older real-only citation.

nodes.title: Compact inclusion alone does not give Siegel containment
nodes.statement: There are inclusions of reductive (even semisimple) ℚ-groups 𝐇 ⊂ 𝐆 with K_H ⊂ K_G for which some 𝐇-Siegel set is not covered by finitely many 𝐆(ℚ)-translates of K_G-Siegel sets; the Cartan compatibility hypothesis of orr-schnell-containment cannot be removed.
hypotheses: The groups and maps are the concrete ones specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the explicit split torus H={[[x,x⁻¹−x],[0,x⁻¹]]}⊂SL₂ and K_G=SO₂. Its orbit in the upper half-plane is (1−y)+iy for y>0.

A rational translate of a standard Siegel strip is bounded above in imaginary part unless the rational matrix is upper triangular; upper-triangular translates stay in a vertical strip of bounded width. No finite family covers this ray.

For the semisimple example use H=ηSO(J)η⁻¹⊂SL₃ from Orr–Schnell §C. The noncompact-intersection root lemma forces the relevant rational translate into the upper parabolic; unipotent boundedness would then imply ηᵀη diagonal, contrary to its displayed matrix. The complete root-intersection lemma is recorded as a refinement.
acceptance: Any definable-morphism interface built on Siegel sets must carry the Cartan compatibility hypothesis.

sources.match: Both counterexamples have K_H⊂K_G but lack the required Cartan compatibility.

nodes.title: Preimages of Siegel sets under orbit maps
nodes.statement: Let 𝐇 ⊂ SL(V) be reductive over ℚ, x_0 ∈ X = SL(V_ℝ)/SO(b_0) with K_H = Stab_{𝐇(ℝ)}(x_0) and the Cartan involution of x_0 stabilising Lie 𝐇, and ι : 𝐇(ℝ)/K_H → X the orbit map. For every Siegel set 𝔖 ⊂ X, ι⁻¹(𝔖) is contained in finitely many Siegel sets of 𝐇(ℝ)/K_H associated to K_H.
hypotheses: as stated
proofSteps: ι⁻¹(𝔖_SL x_0) = (𝔖_SL K_SL ∩ 𝐇(ℝ)) x_0; apply rational-siegel-pullback, whose forward-containment hypothesis is orr-schnell-containment with cartan-subgroup-criterion.
acceptance: For 𝐇 = SL(V) it is trivial.
The Hodge-theoretic specialization (period domains D and the map to positive forms) belongs to DegeneratingHodgeStructures.

sources.match: Siegel sets of the space X of positive forms; the pullback statement is the extraction's item siegel-preimage-under-hodge-form-map, stated here for a general orbit map.

nodes.title: Images of Siegel sets under orbit maps
nodes.statement: In the setting of orbit-map-siegel-preimage, every Siegel set of 𝐇(ℝ)/K_H is mapped by ι into finitely many Siegel sets of X.
hypotheses: as in orbit-map-siegel-preimage
proofSteps: Apply orr-schnell-containment to 𝐇 ⊂ SL(V); Siegel sets of X do not depend on the choice of maximal compact up to rational translates, and c𝔖 for c ∈ SL(V_ℚ) is a Siegel set (real-siegel-translation).
acceptance: For 𝐇 = SO(Q) of an indefinite rational form and x_0 a majorant b_0(v, w) = Q(v, Cw) with C ∈ O(Q)(ℝ) a Weil operator (so the Cartan involution of x_0 stabilises Lie 𝐇), Siegel sets of the symmetric space map into finitely many Siegel sets of positive forms.

sources.match: The ambient Siegel sets; the image statement is the extraction's item siegel-image-under-hodge-form-map, stated for a general orbit map.

nodes.title: Reduced positive forms
nodes.statement: Given an ordered basis e = (e_i) of V_ℚ (integral bases of V_ℤ in BKT), C > 0 and a positive definite symmetric form b on V_ℝ, b is (e, C)-reduced if (1) |b(e_i, e_j)| < C b(e_i, e_i) for all i, j; (2) b(e_i, e_i) < C b(e_j, e_j) for i < j; (3) ∏_i b(e_i, e_i) < C det(b), the Gram determinant in e.
hypotheses: V a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space
e an ordered basis
proofSteps: Define as a predicate on Gram matrices.
acceptance: The identity form is (e, 2)-reduced for the standard basis.
Rescaling e_i by integers changes C by bounded factors.

nodes.title: Reduced forms and Siegel sets
nodes.statement: For an ordered integral basis e and C>0, the set of (e,C)-reduced positive definite forms lies in the image of a GL_n(ℝ) Siegel set in GL_n(ℝ)/O(n), and each such Siegel set has reduced-form image for some C. Restricting to Gram determinant one gives the corresponding statement for SL_n(ℝ)/SO(n); normalize an arbitrary form B by det(B)^−1/n B. Rational bases are handled by the matching rational change of basis.
hypotheses: V_ℤ a lattice in V_ℚ
proofSteps: Write B=NᵀDN by the pinned Cholesky decomposition; positive definiteness gives positive diagonal pivots.

The diagonal-product/determinant inequality bounds the loss between pivots and diagonal entries. The off-diagonal inequalities then bound N, and the ordered diagonal inequalities bound successive pivot ratios.

Conversely bounded N and the chamber ratios imply the three reducedness inequalities with a uniform constant. Scalar normalization leaves all three conditions unchanged, and imposes determinant one. The precise pivot estimates remain a refinement.
acceptance: For n = 2, reduced forms correspond to the standard Siegel set {|x| ≤ c, y ≥ t} in ℍ.

sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Lower bound by diagonal entries
nodes.statement: Let B be a positive definite real symmetric n × n matrix with diagonal d_k = B_kk and D ≥ 1 with ∏_k d_k ≤ D det B. Then for every real vector a and every k, aᵀ B a ≥ a_k² d_k / D.
hypotheses: B positive definite
∏ d_k ≤ D det B
proofSteps: By Cramer's rule and Hadamard's inequality applied to the minor, (B⁻¹)_kk ≤ ∏_{j≠k} d_j / det B ≤ D / d_k.
Cauchy–Schwarz for the inner product B: a_k² = ⟨a, B⁻¹e_k⟩_B² ≤ (aᵀBa)(B⁻¹)_kk.
acceptance: For B diagonal and D = 1 it is the trivial bound.

nodes.title: Transferring off-diagonal bounds to another basis
nodes.statement: Let B be the Gram matrix in an ordered basis e′ of a positive definite form b with |B_ab| ≤ C′ d_a for all a, b, with d_a ≤ C′ d_b for a < b, and ∏ d_a ≤ C′ det B (C′ ≥ 1). For a fixed basis e_i = ∑_a A_ai e′_a put k_i = max{a : A_ai ≠ 0}, m_i = |A_{k_i,i}|, L_i = ∑_a |A_ai|. Then |b(e_i, e_j)| ≤ C′³ L_i L_j m_i⁻² b(e_i, e_i) for all i, j.
hypotheses: as stated
proofSteps: Expand b(e_i,e_j). For every contributing a≤k_i, |B_ab|≤C′d_a≤C′²d_{k_i}, using the ordering for a<k_i and C′≥1. Thus |b(e_i,e_j)|≤C′²L_iL_jd_{k_i}.
Lower-bound b(e_i, e_i) ≥ m_i² d_{k_i}/C′ by gram-diagonal-lower-bound.

nodes.title: Basis change with determinant control
nodes.statement: Let e, e′ be bases of V_ℚ (m = dim V) and C, C′ ≥ 1. If b is (e′, C′)-reduced and ∏_i b(e_i, e_i) ≤ C det(b in e), then b is (σe, C″)-reduced for the ordering σ of e that sorts the values b(e_i, e_i), with C″ depending only on C, C′ and the change-of-basis matrix; hence b lies in one of the m! sets T_{σe,C″}. The printed statement with the fixed ordering e is false.
hypotheses: as stated
proofSteps: Off-diagonal condition (1) from gram-offdiagonal-transfer; (3) is the hypothesis; (2) holds after sorting.

Counterexample to the fixed-order version: e′ = (e_1, e_2) standard, e = (e_2, e_1), b_t = diag(1, t) for t → ∞: each b_t is (e′, 2)-reduced and satisfies (3) in e with C = 2, but condition (2) in the order e would need C″ > t.

nodes.title: Weak approximation
nodes.statement: An affine algebraic group G over F has weak approximation with respect to a finite set S of places if G(F) is dense in G(F_S) = ∏_{v∈S} G(F_v); it has weak approximation if this holds for every finite S.
hypotheses: F a number field
G affine algebraic over F
proofSteps: Define with the topology of AA.1 on G(F_S) (AA.1/adelic-points-split).
acceptance: G_a has weak approximation (weak approximation for F).
μ_2 does not: {±1} is not dense in {±1}^S for |S| ≥ 2.

sources.match: Weak approximation for a variety over a number field is defined as density of its rational points in the product of all local point sets with the product topology, i.e. density in every finite subproduct; nonemptiness is not assumed.

nodes.statement: GL_n, SL_n, G_a and split tori G_m^r over F have weak approximation.
hypotheses: F a number field
proofSteps: G_a: weakApproximation_denseRange.
GL_n and G_m^r: GL_n(F_S) is open in M_n(F_S) and M_n(F) is dense, so GL_n(F) = M_n(F) ∩ GL_n(F_S) is dense.

nodes.title: Weak approximation for simply connected groups
nodes.statement: A connected semisimple simply connected group G over a number field F has weak approximation; more generally (property (⋆)) a torsor under G that has points at all real places has an F-point and satisfies weak approximation.
hypotheses: G semisimple simply connected over F

nodes.title: Torsors under an affine group over a field

It is trivial if X(k) ≠ ∅.
hypotheses: k a field
G affine algebraic over k
proofSteps: Comodule algebras and base change; triviality iff a k-point exists (then X ≅ G).
acceptance: G acting on itself is the trivial torsor.
For G = μ_2 over ℚ and a ∈ ℚ^×, Spec ℚ[x]/(x² − a) is a torsor, trivial iff a is a square in ℚ^× (for a = 0 it is not a torsor).

nodes.title: Tori never have strong approximation for finite S

S finite

nodes.title: Closures of Zariski-dense subgroups are open
nodes.statement: Let G be connected absolutely almost simple over ℚ_p, and Γ⊂G(ℚ_p) a Zariski-dense nondiscrete subgroup. Its closure is open in G(ℚ_p), subject to the recorded p-adic analytic closed-subgroup input. This statement does not extend to arbitrary E/ℚ_p with E-Zariski density alone.
hypotheses: G connected absolutely almost simple over ℚ_p
Γ⊂G(ℚ_p) Zariski dense and nondiscrete
proofSteps: The closure Δ is a p-adic analytic subgroup of positive dimension (Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem; recorded gap).
Its Lie algebra is Ad Γ-invariant, hence Ad G-invariant by Zariski density, hence everything by irreducibility of the adjoint representation of an absolutely almost simple group.
An analytic subgroup with full Lie algebra is open.
acceptance: For SL_2(ℤ) ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p), the closure is SL_2(ℤ_p).
For a proper finite extension E/ℚ_p, SL_2(ℚ_p)⊂SL_2(E) is E-Zariski dense, closed and nondiscrete but not open. Its analytic dimension is 3 rather than 3[E:ℚ_p].

G_S noncompact

nodes.title: Open subgroups of finite covolume have finite index
nodes.statement: If Δ is an open subgroup of a locally compact group H such that H/Δ carries a nonzero finite H-invariant Radon measure, then Δ has finite index in H.
hypotheses: H locally compact
Δ open
The quotient measure is nonzero, finite and Radon
proofSteps: H/Δ is discrete; an invariant measure on a discrete homogeneous space gives every point the same mass c. Compact subsets are finite, so a nonzero Radon measure has c > 0 by inner regularity; then any n points have measure nc ≤ μ(H/Δ) < ∞, so H/Δ is finite.
acceptance: ℤ_p ⊂ ℚ_p is open but ℚ_p/ℤ_p has infinite invariant measure.

sources.match: Exactly the step.

nodes.title: Strong approximation: sufficiency
nodes.statement: Let G be connected, absolutely almost simple and simply connected over a number field F, and S a finite set of places containing the archimedean ones with G_S = ∏_{v∈S} G(F_v) noncompact. Then G has strong approximation with respect to S.
hypotheses: G absolutely almost simple simply connected over F
S ⊇ archimedean places
G_S noncompact
proofSteps: Let H be the closure of G(F)G_S in G(𝔸_F); strong approximation with respect to S means H = G(𝔸_F) (strong-approximation-property).

For every finite v ∉ S at which G is F_v-isotropic, H contains G(F_v) placed at v (isotropic-place-closure). Here simple connectedness enters through the RG2.4 Kneser–Tits finite-index theorem; it enters once more in the last step, through weak approximation for simply connected groups.

The set T of finite v ∉ S at which G is F_v-anisotropic is finite (isotropic-almost-everywhere). H is a closed subgroup containing G_S and every G(F_v) with v ∉ S ∪ T, so it contains G_S × ∏'_{v∉S∪T} G(F_v): finite truncations converge in the restricted-product topology.

Weak approximation (weak-approximation-simply-connected) makes G(F) dense in G_T. For g ∈ G(𝔸_F) and a compact open subgroup W_T ⊂ G_T pick γ ∈ G(F) with γ_T ∈ g_T W_T; then γ⁻¹g is the product of an element of W_T and an element of the group in the previous step, so g ∈ H·W_T. Shrinking W_T gives g ∈ H. No several-place Lie algebra and no anisotropic finite-index elimination is needed.
acceptance: SL_n over ℚ with S = {∞}: SL_n(ℤ) is dense in SL_n(ℤ̂), i.e. SL_n(ℤ) → SL_n(ℤ/N) is surjective.
For SL_1(B), B definite quaternion over ℚ, S = {∞}: G_S is compact and the theorem does not apply.

sources.match: The theorem (sufficiency half).
Where simple connectedness enters (Kneser–Tits).

nodes.title: Strong approximation: necessity
nodes.statement: In the setting of strong-approximation-sufficiency without the hypotheses: if G has strong approximation with respect to S then G_S is noncompact and G is simply connected.
hypotheses: G connected absolutely almost simple over F
S finite
proofSteps: If G_S is compact, G(F) is discrete in G(𝔸) and G_S compact, so G(F) is discrete in G(𝔸^S), which is not discrete; so G(F) is not dense.

If G is not simply connected, let π : G̃ → G be the simply connected cover with kernel a nontrivial finite group scheme; Chebotarev produces infinitely many places v with G(F_v)/π(G̃(F_v)) nontrivial, and the image of G(F) cannot be dense in the corresponding product (Rapinchuk §2.3, Proposition 2.2).
acceptance: PGL_2 over ℚ fails strong approximation for S = {∞}: det modulo squares separates classes.
SL_1(B) with B definite and S = {∞} fails: G_∞ compact.

sources.match: Both necessary conditions.

nodes.title: Strong approximation for semisimple groups
nodes.statement: Let G be connected semisimple simply connected over F and S ⊇ archimedean places finite such that G′(F_S) is noncompact for every F-simple factor G′ of G. Then G(𝔸_F) = G(F)·G(F_S)·U for every compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_F^S); in particular G(F)\G(𝔸_f)/U is a single point when S is the set of archimedean places.
hypotheses: G semisimple simply connected
each F-simple factor noncompact at S
proofSteps: G = ∏ Res_{F_i/F} G_i with G_i absolutely almost simple simply connected (restriction of scalars, AA.1/base-change-adelic).
Apply strong-approximation-sufficiency to each G_i over F_i with the places above S; noncompactness of Res G_i at S is noncompactness of G_i at the places above S.
Density gives G(𝔸^S) = G(F)U.
acceptance: SL_2 over a number field F, S archimedean: class number one for every level.

sources.match: Exactly the statement over ℚ.

nodes.title: Class sets of groups with simply connected derived group
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over F with G^der simply connected and G^der(F_∞) noncompact on each F-simple factor, ν : G → D = G/G^der. For compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}), ν induces a bijection G(F)\G(𝔸_{F,f})/U ≃ ν(G(F))\D(𝔸_{F,f})/ν(U).
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
G^der simply connected
G^der(F_∞) noncompact on each simple factor
proofSteps: Finite adelic surjectivity of ν proves surjectivity on the displayed class sets; the rational image remains ν(G(F)), without replacing it by D(F).
If ν(y)=ν(γ)ν(x)ν(u), then y=γxhu with h∈G^der(𝔸_f).
Strong approximation for G^der applied to the conjugated compact open x(U∩G^der)x⁻¹ puts h into a rational-derived translate of U∩G^der, proving injectivity.
acceptance: For GL_n: GL_n(F)\GL_n(𝔸_f)/GL_n(Ô) ≅ F^×\𝔸_f^×/Ô^× = Cl(F).
For B^× with B definite over ℚ, G^der = SL_1(B) is compact at ∞ and the hypothesis fails; indeed class numbers of definite quaternion orders exceed the narrow class number in general.

sources.match: The reduced-norm bijection on class sets, here for any G with simply connected noncompact derived group.

nodes.title: Neat elements
nodes.statement: An automorphism α of a finite-dimensional vector space over a subfield of ℂ is neat if its eigenvalues in ℂ generate a torsion-free subgroup of ℂ^×. An element g ∈ G(F) of a linear algebraic group over a number field F is neat if ρ(g) is neat for one faithful F-representation ρ; a subgroup of G(F) is neat if all its elements are.
hypotheses: F a number field with a fixed embedding τ : F → ℂ; the notion does not depend on τ, since an automorphism of ℂ carries one eigenvalue group isomorphically onto the other. It is weaker than neatness of g as an element of (Res_{F/ℚ}G)(ℚ), whose eigenvalues include all Galois conjugates: √2 ∈ G_m(ℚ(√2)) is neat, but ±√2 generate a group containing −1
G linear algebraic

The group representation is algebraic and faithful, rather than merely injective as a map on F-rational points. In Hopf coordinates it is induced by a surjective GL_n-coordinate morphism O(GL_n)→O(G).
proofSteps: First define neatness relative to a specified faithful closed algebraic representation, using its eigenvalue subgroup.
The theorem neat-representation-independence subsequently proves that this predicate is independent of the chosen representation; it is not a prerequisite of the definition.
acceptance: No nontrivial element of finite order is neat.
diag(2, 1/2) ∈ SL_2(ℚ) is neat; diag(−1, −1) is not.

nodes.title: Neatness does not depend on the representation
nodes.statement: If ρ(g) is neat for one faithful representation ρ of G then σ(g) is neat for every representation σ of G defined over a subfield of ℂ.
hypotheses: G a finite-type linear algebraic group over the number field F

ρ is a faithful algebraic representation (a closed immersion), σ is an algebraic representation, and the compared complex point actions use the same embedding F→ℂ. Arbitrary homomorphisms of the abstract rational-point group are excluded.
proofSteps: By algebraic-tensor-eigenvalues the eigenvalue subgroup for σ(g) is a subgroup of that for the chosen faithful algebraic ρ(g).
A subgroup of a torsion-free group is torsion free. Base-field extension does not change the abstract multiplicative relations between eigenvalues.

nodes.title: Neatness is stable under subgroups, conjugation and homomorphisms

proofSteps: Subgroups: by definition.
Conjugation preserves eigenvalues.
Homomorphisms: σ ∘ φ is a representation of G; apply neat-representation-independence.
acceptance: The image of a neat subgroup of SL_2(ℚ) in PGL_2(ℚ) is neat.

nodes.title: A one-prime criterion for neatness
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G ↪ GL_n be a faithful representation over ℚ (after restriction of scalars) and U ⊂ G(𝔸_f) compact open. If for some prime p ≥ 3 the projection of ρ(U) to GL_n(ℚ_p) lies in 1 + p M_n(ℤ_p) (for p = 2, in 1 + 4M_n(ℤ_2)), then U is neat.
hypotheses: ρ faithful
U compact open
p ≥ 3 (or p = 2 with level 4)
proofSteps: For γ ∈ G(ℚ) ∩ xUx⁻¹, ρ(γ) is conjugate in GL_n(ℚ_p) to an element of x_p ρ(U_p) x_p⁻¹, whose eigenvalues λ in ℚ̄_p satisfy |λ − 1|_p ≤ p⁻¹ (resp. 4⁻¹) because they are eigenvalues of conjugates of elements of 1 + pM_n(ℤ_p).
The multiplicative group {λ : |λ − 1|_p < p^{-1/(p−1)}} of ℚ̄_p contains no nontrivial root of unity, and it contains the group generated by such eigenvalues.
Embedding the eigenvalue group (inside ℚ̄^×) in both ℂ^× and ℚ̄_p^× gives the same abstract group, so it is torsion free.
acceptance: U(3) ⊂ GL_2(ℤ̂) is neat; U(2) is not (it contains −1).

nodes.title: Neat levels exist
nodes.statement: Every compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) contains a neat normal open subgroup of finite index; every arithmetic subgroup of G(F) contains a neat subgroup of finite index defined by congruence conditions (Borel).
hypotheses: G linear algebraic over F
proofSteps: After restriction of scalars take a faithful algebraic ℚ-representation and one prime p≥3. The projection of U is compact and has a stable ℤ_p-lattice.
The inverse image of the identity modulo p on this lattice is normal and open in U, with finite index by compactness.

Choose L = hℤ_p^n with h ∈ GL_n(ℚ) (possible since GL_n(ℚ) is dense in GL_n(ℚ_p) and the stabilizer of a lattice is open), so that h⁻¹ρh is again a faithful ℚ-representation whose p-component on this subgroup lies in 1 + pM_n(ℤ_p); the one-prime criterion then makes it neat for every rational conjugate intersection (its proof only uses eigenvalues, which conjugation does not change). Intersect an arithmetic subgroup with the resulting congruence level.
acceptance: GL_2(ℤ̂) ⊃ U(3) neat of index #GL_2(ℤ/3) = 48.

nodes.title: Finite-index bound for level changes
nodes.statement: For K′ ≤ K of finite index N, every fibre of H\G/K′ → H\G/K has at most N elements; if H\G/K is finite of cardinality h then H\G/K′ is finite of cardinality at most Nh. No normality, freeness or neatness is assumed.
hypotheses: K′ ≤ K, [K : K′] = N finite
proofSteps: fibreSurj is a surjection from a set of size N.
The fine quotient is the disjoint union of its fibres over a finite base.
acceptance: For H = 1 equality holds; for H = G and N > 1 it is strict.

proofSteps: If g′ = h g (a k a⁻¹) then g′a = h (g a) k; the inverse similarly.
acceptance: a = 1 gives the identity.

nodes.title: Index of product subgroups with finite exceptional support
nodes.statement: For groups H_v with subgroups S_v ≤ H_v equal to H_v outside a finite set B and of finite index for v ∈ B, (∏ H_v)/(∏ S_v) ≃ ∏_{v∈B} H_v/S_v and [∏ H_v : ∏ S_v] = ∏_{v∈B} [H_v : S_v]; in particular for compact open product levels in G(𝔸_f), [∏ K_v : ∏ K′_v] = ∏_v [K_v : K′_v].
hypotheses: S_v = H_v outside finite B
proofSteps: Map a coset to its components; coordinatewise membership; lift finitely many representatives with identity elsewhere.

nodes.title: Level quotients
nodes.statement: For compact open U ⊂ G(𝔸_{F,f}) and a closed subgroup K_∞ ⊂ G(F_∞) (for example a maximal compact subgroup times A_G(ℝ)^0, or trivial), the level quotient is X_U = G(F)\G(𝔸_F)/K_∞U with the quotient topology, together with the right action of G(𝔸_f) by Hecke translation X_{gUg⁻¹} ≃ X_U, [x] ↦ [xg].
hypotheses: F a number field
G a connected reductive group over F
U compact open
K_∞ closed
proofSteps: Quotient of G(𝔸) by the left action of G(F) and right action of K_∞U.
Right translation by g carries the K_∞(gUg⁻¹)-orbits to K_∞U-orbits.
acceptance: For K_∞ = 1, X_U ≃ ⊔ Γ_i\G(F_∞) (AA.3/component-decomposition).

For GL_2/ℚ and principal K(N), K∞=ℝ^×SO(2) gives φ(N) copies of Γ(N)\ℍ. With K∞=ℝ^×O(2), the negative-determinant involution identifies the pair of half-plane components, giving determinant classes (ℤ/N)^×/{±1}, hence φ(N)/2 components for N≥3.
